title: [DEMO / SYNTHETIC] International Reference Pricing (IRP) Principles & Global Standards
content: International Reference Pricing (IRP), also known as external reference pricing (ERP), is the practice of using the price of a pharmaceutical product in one or several countries to derive a benchmark or reference price for the purpose of setting or negotiating the price in a target country. Key design parameters of an IRP system include the composition of the reference country basket, the formula used (e.g., minimum, average of lowest three, median), the price type referenced (ex-factory, wholesale, or public retail), and whether adjustments are made for purchasing power parity (PPP) or exchange rate volatility. Official methodologies vary widely across jurisdictions and require strict validation before execution.

title: [DEMO / SYNTHETIC] Ecuador Pharmaceutical Reference Pricing Framework (Decree Overview)
source_authority: DEMO / Simulated Ecuador Ministry of Health
content: In Ecuador, maximum regulated ceiling prices for strategic medicines are established pursuant to executive decree and health authority directives. The regulatory system categorizes medicines by therapeutic importance and market competition. While international reference baskets are consulted by technical committees, the exact mathematical formula, currency normalization rules, and mandatory adjustments must adhere strictly to the certified technical decree published by the National Pricing Council (CONASA / ARCSA). Note: For the Roche Pricing Intelligence prototype, calculations remain in 'NOT CALCULATED — Official Roche methodology pending' status until certified by the Roche pricing team.

title: [DEMO / SYNTHETIC] Colombia Price Reporting & Reference Pricing Mechanism (Circular Overview)
source_authority: DEMO / Simulated Ministry of Health Colombia
source_url: NO_ROCHE_APPROVED_SOURCE (Inventory observation: 'Fijan precios máximos al distribuidor')
content: Colombia's National Commission on Prices of Medicines and Medical Devices (CNPMD) regulates medicine prices through circulars. The system relies on mandatory quarterly price reporting by pharmaceutical manufacturers, distributors, and institutional providers into the SISMED database. International reference pricing in Colombia evaluates an international reference basket comparing ex-factory and institutional procurement prices. Medicines with high expenditure impact or limited market contestability are subjected to administrative price ceilings (Precio Máximo de Venta).

title: [DEMO / SYNTHETIC] Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) in Pharmaceutical Price Comparisons
content: Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) conversion adjusts nominal prices to reflect relative differences in the domestic purchasing power and cost of living between countries. In pharmaceutical economics, applying PPP adjustments is debated: while it normalizes affordability relative to local economic output (GDP per capita), manufacturers operate in global supply chains with input costs denominated in hard currencies (USD, EUR, CHF). Unverified PPP formulas should never be used to establish statutory price caps without explicit regulatory authorization.

title: [DEMO / SYNTHETIC] WHO Guidelines on Country Pharmaceutical Pricing Policies
content: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides global guidance on pharmaceutical pricing policies. Guideline recommendations include: 1) Countries should establish transparent, objective criteria when selecting reference countries for external reference pricing; 2) Consideration should be given to hidden discounts, rebates, and managed entry agreements which distort list prices; 3) IRP should be combined with other pricing strategies such as internal reference pricing, cost-plus analysis, or value-based assessment rather than used in isolation.
